title: Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search via Data-Adaptive Parameter Adjustment in Hierarchical Navigable Small Graphs
problem: Hierarchical Navigable Small World graph algorithms use static parameters (connection count M and search depth ef) that do not adapt to variations in data density and dimensionality, causing suboptimal performance across diverse datasets.
motivation: HNSW is widely deployed in recommendation, vision, and NLP applications but static parameter tuning limits efficiency across diverse data characteristics.
method: Proposes Dynamic HNSW with data-adaptive parameter adjustment algorithms; automatically tunes M (connections per node) and ef (search depth) based on local data density and dataset dimensionality to optimize graph construction and search efficiency.
key_novelty: Adaptive parameter tuning algorithm for HNSW based on local data density and global dimensionality.
contributions: Analysis of HNSW parameter sensitivity to data density and dimensionality
Adaptive M and ef adjustment algorithm
Graph build time reduction up to 33.11%
Memory usage reduction up to 32.44% with comparable recall
limitations: Detailed recall-precision curves not presented; computational overhead of adaptive algorithm not discussed.
